decisions.reason: The word first meant freedom of speech. In this letter it is the confidence of a child before God, now (3:21; 5:14) and when Christ appears (2:28).

decisions.choice: that one: Jesus
decisions.reason: In this letter ἐκεῖνος used of a person regularly means Jesus (2:6; 3:3, 5, 7, 16).

decisions.choice: as he is, so are we: believers already share his standing with the Father and live as he lived, while still in this world
alternatives: we are sinless as he is
decisions.reason: Jesus is loved by the Father and remains in him; those who remain in love share that standing, and are to walk as he walked (2:6; 3:2-3). This is why they need not fear the judgment. The letter does not claim they are without sin (1:8) or equal to him.

decisions.choice: boldness (L); confidence (B); be confident (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the root sense of free, bold speech; Balanced and Readable give its sense here (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: has been perfected (L); has been brought to completion (B); has done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:12.

decisions.choice: Jesus; even now, here in this world
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus (meaning decision m4) and stresses that this is true already, before the day of judgment.

decisions.choice: uhuru (L); ujasiri (B); kusimama bila hofu (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:28, 3:21 and 5:14: freedom to stand before someone without fear or shame (m3). The same three words are kept at the three levels.

decisions.choice: "담대함" (L), "담대하다" (B), "두려움 없이" (R) for confidence; "그분이 계신 것처럼" with the honorific for Jesus
decisions.reason: Confidence is freedom to stand before someone without fear or shame (meaning decision), the same word as 2:28 and 3:21. The meaning decision reads "as he is, so are we" as believers already sharing his standing with the Father, and footnotes it; Korean keeps the short comparison at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: φόβος οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ, ἀλλ’ ἡ τελεία ἀγάπη ἔξω βάλλει τὸν φόβον, ὅτι ὁ φόβος κόλασιν ἔχει, ὁ δὲ φοβούμενος οὐ τετελείωται ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Fear not is in the love, but the perfect love out casts the fear, because the fear punishment has, and the [one] fearing not has been perfected in the love.

en.L: Fear is not in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear has punishment, and the one who fears has not been perfected in love.
en.B: Love has no room for fear; instead, complete love throws fear out, because fear has to do with punishment, and anyone who is afraid has not been brought to completion in love.
en.R: Where there is love, there is no fear. Love that is complete pushes fear out. Fear comes from expecting to be punished. So if someone is afraid, love has not yet done its full work in {{gender:them|him}}.

fr.L: Il n’y a pas de crainte dans l’amour, mais l’amour parfait jette dehors la crainte, parce que la crainte comporte un châtiment, et celui qui craint n’a pas été rendu parfait dans l’amour.
fr.B: L’amour ne laisse aucune place à la peur ; au contraire, l’amour accompli chasse la peur, car la peur est liée au châtiment, et celui qui a peur n’est pas parvenu à l’accomplissement dans l’amour.
fr.R: Là où il y a de l’amour, il n’y a pas de peur. L’amour complet chasse la peur. La peur vient de ce qu’on s’attend à être puni. Alors, si quelqu’un a peur, c’est que l’amour n’a pas encore accompli en lui toute son œuvre.

es.L: En el amor no hay temor, sino que el amor perfecto echa fuera el temor, porque el temor tiene [que ver con el] castigo, y el que teme no ha sido perfeccionado en el amor.
es.B: El amor no deja lugar al temor; al contrario, el amor pleno echa fuera el temor, porque el temor tiene que ver con el castigo, y quien tiene miedo no ha llegado a la plenitud en el amor.
es.R: Donde hay amor, no hay miedo. El amor completo empuja el miedo hacia afuera. El miedo viene de esperar un castigo. Así que, si alguien tiene miedo, el amor todavía no ha hecho toda su obra en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.

sw.L: Hofu haipo katika upendo, bali upendo ulio kamili huifukuza hofu nje, kwa sababu hofu inahusiana na adhabu, na anayeogopa hajakamilishwa katika upendo.
sw.B: Upendo hauna nafasi ya hofu; badala yake, upendo kamili huifukuza hofu, kwa sababu hofu inahusiana na adhabu, na yeyote anayeogopa hajafikia lengo la upendo.
sw.R: Palipo na upendo, hapana hofu. Upendo ulio kamili huisukuma hofu nje. Hofu hutokana na kutarajia kuadhibiwa. Kwa hiyo mtu akiwa na hofu, upendo bado haujafanya kazi yake kikamilifu ndani yake.

ko.L: 사랑 안에는 두려움이 없습니다. 오히려 완전한 사랑은 두려움을 밖으로 내쫓습니다. 두려움은 형벌과 관계가 있기 때문입니다. 두려워하는 사람은 사랑 안에서 완전하게 되지 못했습니다.
ko.B: 사랑 안에는 두려움이 자리할 곳이 없습니다. 오히려 완전한 사랑은 두려움을 내쫓습니다. 두려움은 형벌과 관계가 있기 때문입니다. 두려워하는 사람은 아직 사랑 안에서 완성되지 못했습니다.
ko.R: 사랑이 있는 곳에는 두려움이 없습니다. 완전한 사랑은 두려움을 밀어냅니다. 두려움은 벌을 받으리라는 생각에서 나옵니다. 그러니 두려워하는 사람 안에서는 사랑이 아직 할 일을 다 이루지 못한 것입니다.

decisions.choice: fear: dread of God's judgment and punishment
decisions.reason: The context is the day of judgment (4:17). The fear driven out is the dread of someone who expects to be condemned, not the reverent fear of God that Scripture commends elsewhere (Proverbs 1:7; 1 Peter 2:17).

decisions.choice: complete: love that has reached its goal
decisions.reason: The adjective belongs to the same word family as "brought to completion" in 4:12, 17 and at the end of this verse.

decisions.choice: fear has to do with punishment: it looks ahead to punishment and already feels its weight
decisions.reason: κόλασιν means punishment (as in Matthew 25:46). Fear is bound up with it: the one who fears is thinking of punishment and already suffers from the thought. The older rendering "torment" takes the second half of this.

decisions.choice: the one who fears has not been brought to completion in love: love has not yet reached its goal in them
decisions.reason: The perfect describes a present state. Fear shows that God's love has not yet done its full work; it is a call to rest in that love, not a verdict.

decisions.choice: Love has no room for fear (B); Where there is love, there is no fear (R)
alternatives: There is no fear in love
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense of the opening clause in natural wording.

decisions.choice: perfect, perfected (L); complete, brought to completion (B); complete, done its full work (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:12 and 4:17.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Someone" is anyone; the pronoun takes the gender setting. Literal and Balanced need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: la crainte (L); la peur (B, R)
decisions.reason: The fear meant is dread of judgment and punishment (m1). French "crainte" also names the reverent fear of God, which this verse does not reject; Literal keeps it as the word nearest the Greek, and Balanced and Readable say "peur", which can only mean dread. Readable's "en lui" refers back to the generic "quelqu’un" and takes no gender span.

decisions.choice: temor (L, B); miedo (R)
decisions.reason: The fear here is dread of judgment (meaning decision m1). "Temor" is the fuller word; Readable says the everyday "miedo".

decisions.choice: hofu; kuogopa
decisions.reason: The fear is dread of God's judgment and punishment (m1). "Hofu" is that dread; "woga" is closer to timidity. The verb "kuogopa" belongs to the same idea.

records.literal_gloss: We love, because he first loved us.

en.L: We love, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} first loved us.
en.B: We love because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved us first.
en.R: We love because God loved us first.

fr.L: Nous, nous aimons, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a aimés le premier.
fr.B: Nous aimons parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a aimés le premier.
fr.R: Nous aimons parce que Dieu nous a aimés le premier.

es.L: Nosotros amamos, porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos amó primero.
es.B: Nosotros amamos porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos amó primero.
es.R: Nosotros amamos porque Dios nos amó primero.

sw.L: Sisi tunapenda, kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alitupenda kwanza.
sw.B: Tunapenda kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alitupenda kwanza.
sw.R: Tunapenda kwa sababu Mungu alitupenda kwanza.

ko.L: 우리가 사랑하는 것은 그분이 먼저 우리를 사랑하셨기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 사랑하는 것은 그분이 우리를 먼저 사랑하셨기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 우리가 사랑하는 것은 하나님께서 우리를 먼저 사랑하셨기 때문입니다.

decisions.choice: we love: a statement
alternatives: let us love (a call, as in 4:7)
decisions.reason: In the present tense the statement and the call have the same form. The ὅτι clause gives a reason, which suits a statement of where our love comes from, but a call is possible.

decisions.choice: we love, with no object (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts, including Codex Alexandrinus and Codex Vaticanus, have no object. Codex Sinaiticus adds "God", and most later manuscripts add "him". The additions narrow the love to love for God; without them it includes love for one another, which 4:20-21 goes on to speak of. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: he first: God's love comes first and makes ours possible
decisions.reason: As in 4:10: not that we loved God, but that he loved us. αὐτὸς means God.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: tunapenda, with no object
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT text has "we love" with no object (m2), so Swahili adds no object marker: "tunapenda", not "tunampenda" (we love him).

decisions.choice: "우리가 사랑하는 것은" (a statement)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "we love" as a statement and footnotes the reading "let us love"; Korean must choose, and follows the meaning decision.

source.text: ἐάν τις εἴπῃ ὅτι Ἀγαπῶ τὸν θεόν, καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ μισῇ, ψεύστης ἐστίν· ὁ γὰρ μὴ ἀγαπῶν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν ἑώρακεν, τὸν θεὸν ὃν οὐχ ἑώρακεν οὐ δύναται ἀγαπᾶν.

records.literal_gloss: If anyone says, I love God, and the brother of him hates, a liar he is; for the [one] not loving the brother of him whom he has seen, God whom not he has seen not is able to love.

en.L: If anyone says, "I love God," and hates {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}, {{gender:they are|he is}} a liar; for the one who does not love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} seen, cannot love God, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} not seen.
en.B: If someone says, "I love God," but hates {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, that person is a liar. For anyone who does not love {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} seen, is not able to love God, whom {{gender:they have|he has}} not seen.
en.R: Suppose someone says, "I love God," but hates a fellow believer. That person is a liar. People who do not love a fellow believer they have seen cannot love God, whom they have never seen.

fr.L: Si quelqu’un dit : « J’aime Dieu » et qu’il haïsse {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}}, c’est un menteur ; car celui qui n’aime pas {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur, qu’il a vus|son frère, qu’il a vu}}, ne peut pas aimer Dieu, qu’il n’a pas vu.
fr.B: Si quelqu’un dit : « J’aime Dieu », mais qu’il haïsse {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|son frère}}, celui-là est un menteur. Car celui qui n’aime pas {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|son frère}} qu’il voit n’est pas capable d’aimer Dieu, qu’il ne voit pas.
fr.R: Imaginons que quelqu’un dise : « J’aime Dieu », mais qu’il haïsse un frère ou une sœur dans la foi. Celui-là est un menteur. Celui qui n’aime pas un frère ou une sœur dans la foi, qu’il voit, ne peut pas aimer Dieu, qu’il n’a jamais vu.

es.L: Si alguno dice: «Amo a Dios», y odia a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}, es mentiroso; porque el que no ama a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}, a quien ha visto, no puede amar a Dios, a quien no ha visto.
es.B: Si alguien dice: «Amo a Dios», pero odia a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana|su hermano}}, esa persona es mentirosa. Porque quien no ama a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana|su hermano}}, a quien ha visto, no es capaz de amar a Dios, a quien no ha visto.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien dice: «Amo a Dios», pero odia a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}}. Esa persona es mentirosa. Quien no ama a {{gender:un hermano o una hermana en la fe|un hermano en la fe}} a quien ha visto, no puede amar a Dios, a quien nunca ha visto.

sw.L: Ikiwa mtu yeyote atasema, "Nampenda Mungu," huku akimchukia ndugu yake, huyo ni mwongo; kwa kuwa asiyempenda ndugu yake aliyemwona, Mungu asiyemwona hawezi kumpenda.
sw.B: Mtu akisema, "Ninampenda Mungu," lakini anamchukia ndugu yake, mtu huyo ni mwongo. Kwa maana yeyote asiyempenda ndugu yake aliyemwona, hawezi kumpenda Mungu ambaye hajamwona.
sw.R: Huenda mtu akasema, "Ninampenda Mungu," lakini anamchukia mwamini mwenzake. Mtu huyo ni mwongo. Watu wasiompenda mwamini mwenzao wanayemwona hawawezi kumpenda Mungu ambaye hawajawahi kumwona.

ko.L: 누가 "나는 하나님을 사랑한다" 하고 말하면서 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 미워하면, 그는 거짓말쟁이입니다. 눈에 보이는 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 보이지 않는 하나님을 사랑할 수 없기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 누가 "나는 하나님을 사랑한다" 하고 말하면서 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 미워한다면, 그 사람은 거짓말쟁이입니다. 자기가 본 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 자기가 보지 못한 하나님을 사랑할 수 없습니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 "나는 하나님을 사랑한다" 하고 말하면서 믿음의 식구를 미워한다고 해 봅시다. 그 사람은 거짓말쟁이입니다. 자기 눈으로 본 믿음의 식구를 사랑하지 않는 사람은 한 번도 본 적이 없는 하나님을 사랑할 수 없습니다.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman, a member of God's family
decisions.reason: In this letter the brother is a fellow child of God (3:10-17; 5:1-2). The word is masculine in form but covers sisters as well. Love for all people is not denied, but this is the immediate sense.

decisions.choice: hate: refuse love and help, not only feel dislike
decisions.reason: In 3:15-17 hating a brother is set beside closing one's heart to a brother in need.

decisions.choice: a liar: one whose claim is contradicted by life
decisions.reason: As in 1:6 and 2:4: a claim to know or love God is tested by how one lives.

decisions.choice: an argument from the easier to the harder: the seen brother and the unseen God
decisions.reason: If one does not love the person one can see, love for the God no one has seen (4:12) is impossible. The perfect "has seen" means seen and known.

decisions.choice: cannot love (SBLGNT)
alternatives: how can he love God? (πῶς instead of οὐ)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, including some early ones and most later ones, put the end as a question, "how can he love God...?"; others, including Codex Vaticanus, have the statement. The meaning is the same. A reviewer must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:they are|he is}}; {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: The brother may be a man or a woman (meaning decision m1), and the speaker is anyone. Balanced uses "that person", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: a fellow believer
decisions.reason: Readable says who is meant (meaning decision m1); the wording is already inclusive and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: is not able to love
decisions.reason: The verb means "is not able"; Balanced says so in full, Literal and Readable use "cannot".

decisions.choice: {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur, qu’il a vus|son frère, qu’il a vu}} (L); qu’il voit (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English needs spans for the pronouns; French does not, but the past participle after "que" must agree with the brother or sister. Literal keeps the Greek perfect and puts the participle under the same setting as the noun (style guide 7); Balanced and Readable say "qu’il voit", which needs no agreement and keeps the contrast between the brother who is seen and God who is not (m4).

decisions.choice: {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}; no span for "they are|he is", "they have|he has"
decisions.reason: As in 2:9: the singular "hermano" takes the gender setting. Spanish leaves the subject of "es mentiroso" and "ha visto" unsaid, so the English pronoun spans need no counterpart.

decisions.choice: ndugu yake (L, B); mwamini mwenzake (R); no gender span
alternatives: ndugu yake wa kiume au wa kike
decisions.reason: As in 2:9: "ndugu" already means a brother or sister in God's family (m1), and the verbs do not mark sex, so the English spans have no Swahili counterpart, here or in verse 21.

source.text: καὶ ταύτην τὴν ἐντολὴν ἔχομεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν θεὸν ἀγαπᾷ καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And this the commandment we have from him, that the [one] loving God love also the brother of him.

en.L: And this commandment we have from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: that the one who loves God should love {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}} also.
en.B: And this is the command we have received from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: the one who loves God is to love {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}} as well.
en.R: God has given us this command: anyone who loves God has to love other believers too.

fr.L: Et ce commandement, nous le tenons de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : que celui qui aime Dieu aime aussi {{gender:son frère ou sa sœur|son frère}}.
fr.B: Et voici le commandement que nous avons reçu de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} : celui qui aime Dieu doit aimer aussi {{gender:un frère ou une sœur|son frère}}.
fr.R: Dieu nous a donné ce commandement : celui qui aime Dieu doit aussi aimer ses frères et sœurs dans la foi.

es.L: Y este mandamiento tenemos de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: que el que ama a Dios ame también a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}.
es.B: Y este es el mandamiento que hemos recibido de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: quien ama a Dios debe amar también a {{gender:su hermano o hermana|su hermano}}.
es.R: Dios nos ha dado este mandato: todo el que ama a Dios tiene que amar también a los demás creyentes.

sw.L: Na amri hii tunayo kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, kwamba anayempenda Mungu ampende pia ndugu yake.
sw.B: Na hii ndiyo amri tuliyopokea kutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}: anayempenda Mungu anapaswa kumpenda ndugu yake pia.
sw.R: Mungu ametupa amri hii: kila anayempenda Mungu lazima awapende waamini wengine pia.

ko.L: 그리고 우리는 그분에게서 이 계명을 받았습니다. 하나님을 사랑하는 사람은 자기 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}도 사랑해야 한다는 것입니다.
ko.B: 우리가 그분에게서 받은 계명은 이것입니다. 하나님을 사랑하는 사람은 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}도 사랑해야 합니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 우리에게 이 계명을 주셨습니다. 하나님을 사랑하는 사람은 다른 믿음의 식구들도 사랑해야 합니다.

decisions.choice: from him: from God, who gave the command through Jesus
decisions.reason: God is the subject of 4:20, and in 3:23 the command to love one another is God's. Jesus gave it to his disciples (John 13:34), so the two are not in tension.

decisions.choice: that: gives what the command says
decisions.reason: The clause states the content of the command.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow believer, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 4:20.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their brother or sister|his brother}}; {{gender:a brother or sister|his brother}}
decisions.reason: As in 4:20.

decisions.choice: God has given us; other believers
alternatives: we have from him; his brother
decisions.reason: Readable names God (meaning decision m1) and uses an inclusive plural that needs no setting.

decisions.choice: commandment (L); command (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Command" is the everyday word.
